entities.name: Masjid Al-Abdul Razak
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Masjid Al-Abdul Razak is a mosque in Singapore, one of approximately 70 mosques serving Singapore's Muslim community (approximately 15% of the population, predominantly Malay-Muslim). The mosque reflects Singapore's distinctive position as a prosperous multi-religious city-state in which Islam's institutional presence is carefully managed through the Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS, Islamic Religious Council of Singapore), which oversees mosques, zakat (Islamic tax), halal certification, and Islamic education.

Singapore's approach to mosque governance is distinctive: MUIS administers a mosque-building fund (MBMF, Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund) through monthly salary deductions from Muslim workers, systematically funding mosque construction and management. This institutional approach to Islamic community organization — combining state oversight with community funding — has made Singapore's mosque system one of the most efficiently managed in the world.

Singapore's Malay-Muslim community has historically faced particular challenges: as an ethnic and religious minority in a majority-Chinese, secular state, Malay-Singaporeans have had to navigate between Malay cultural identity, Islamic religious identity, and Singaporean civic integration. Singaporean mosques, including Masjid Al-Abdul Razak, function as community anchors for this navigation — providing Islamic education, social services, and cultural programming that supports Malay-Muslim identity within Singapore's multicultural framework.
